text.content: Lodin was, until recently, Prince of Chicago for well over a century, ruling with a firm and pragmatic @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} hand through his brood and elder allies. He built the modern city's Kindred infrastructure, established the Elysium and its Traditions, and waged decades of quiet war against anarchs and socialists (chiefly Modius of Gary) who challenged Ventrue dominance. During the werewolf incursion that devastated Chicago's Kindred population (compatible with Under a Blood Red Moon), Lodin was torn apart by Garou claws, his corpse the grim final symbol of the city's fall. His death has left a power vacuum: the primogen council squabbles over succession, Balthazar (his former Sheriff) is angling for the throne, and no one has yet been confirmed as the new Prince. Many of the city's Kindred do not yet know that Lodin's rule was itself a proxy front in the ancient, secret war between the torpid Methuselahs Helena and Menele.

Helena is a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} Methuselah of tremendous antiquity, an ancient rival of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} Methuselah Menele since their shared history in Carthage, Pompeii, and the New World conquests. For roughly 250 years she and Menele have both lain in torpor following a climactic battle near Fort Dearborn, directing Chicago's Kindred through Dominate, Blood Bonds, and unwitting proxies — Lodin and his @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} brood chief among Helena's tools. In 1990, Helena rose from torpor, weakened and disoriented by a changed world, and has moved cautiously ever since, searching for Menele's resting place while rebuilding her influence over the primogen. She operates under the guise or byname "Portia" among those few who suspect her true nature. Almost no one in the city — not even Critias, the primogen's eldest Brujah, who is secretly Blood Bound to Menele — realizes both Methuselahs are real and active participants in Chicago's political disasters.

Critias is the eldest and most respected member of Chicago's primogen, a 5th-generation @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} Embraced in ancient Athens by Menele himself, who was drawn to the Sophist philosopher's skill at debate. Unknown to Critias, he was Blood Bound to Menele centuries ago and has unwittingly served as his sire's primary instrument in Chicago ever since, believing his own political maneuvering (including his secret support of Annabelle Triabell and the anarchs during the Council Wars) to be entirely his own idea. Critias is a professor at Chicago University, mentoring brilliant male students (he is unabashedly sexist and prefers attractive young intellectual men as both proteges and victims), and dreams of establishing a democratic Kindred government in the city. Following Lodin's death, he cautiously tests whether the political climate might finally support such reform, believing (accurately) that his long patience must continue a while longer.

Annabelle Triabell is a leading @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} on Chicago's primogen council. Though not a particularly potent political force in her own right, hers was the deciding vote that split the council against Prince Lodin in early 1983, sparking the internal conflict remembered as the Council Wars. She secretly groomed and supported Maldavis, the anarch leader who nearly toppled Lodin's rule, receiving unknowing backing from both Critias and Helena — each of whom believed they alone were pulling Annabelle's strings. In truth, Menele orchestrated the entire affair to make Helena believe she had gained control of the primogen. Annabelle remains a quietly influential and dangerously underestimated player in the city's ongoing power struggles.

Modius has ruled neighboring Gary, Indiana as its Prince for decades, having built his power base leading the socialist and trade-union movement against both mortal industrial barons and Chicago's corrupt @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue}-dominated political machine. His decades-long war against Prince Lodin defined much of Chicago's Kindred history: he was allied for a time with the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} Alexis Blanc, Balthazar, and Marc Levesque, until Balthazar's betrayal (staking and burning Alexis alive) crippled Modius's momentum and let Lodin recover. Modius still commands loyalty among Chicago's anarchs and socialists as a symbol of resistance to Ventrue authority, and Gary itself remains an anarch-friendly refuge just outside Chicago proper.

Abraham DuSable is a distinguished Black @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} whose family believed him murdered by the Ku Klux Klan shortly after World War I. In 1980, his mortal great-niece Carol Davis recognized him in a jazz club — he had not visibly aged in sixty years. Panicked and torn between fear of exposure and a desire he had never before felt, DuSable lost control of his Beast and nearly drained her, then fled after giving her a single drop of his vitae in a fit of guilt. The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} information broker Dickie, who had already been watching DuSable on suspicion of Tremere manipulation in city politics, discovered the dying Davis and used the incident as leverage. DuSable's secret and its fallout remain a live thread in the Tremere chantry's dealings with the wider city, and his family connection is a rare vulnerability for a clan that prizes secrecy above all.

Khalid al-Rashid was a Muslim warlord during the Crusades whose reputation for atrocity was extreme even by the standards of that brutal age — a reputation that drew the attention of a Cainite who Embraced him amid the bloodshed of the Holy Land. Khalid went berserk upon realizing what he had become, savaging his own men before fleeing into the desert, where a reclusive Jewish hermit saved him from the sun and sheltered him for a month while he studied Kabbalistic mysticism. That study transformed him, and he emerged from the desert a changed Cainite. Now resident in Chicago, Khalid is a solitary, mystically inclined @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} whose Kabbalah-inflected worldview and violent past make him an unpredictable, dangerous factor in the city's Kindred affairs.

Gengis is one of Chicago's most visible anarch die-hards — an impulsive, reflexive rebel Embraced in the late 1960s by a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} passing through the city, who moved on soon after and left Gengis to find his own way. He was one of the city's first punks in the 1970s and has never abandoned the aesthetic, hating the elders on principle and living for a good fight, especially one that draws blood. He has not fully processed his own immortality and shows little concern for his own safety. Despite his rebellious posturing, Gengis is, in truth, deeply conformist to punk and anarch values, and will naturally gravitate toward and emulate anyone he perceives as a strong, "cool" leader — a trait Storytellers can use to pull him into a coterie's orbit or set him against it.

Kevin Jackson is a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} who, with Lodin's backing, seized control of a South Side public-housing project and transformed it into one of the most heavily fortified Kindred domains in the city — known among Kindred as "Blood turf," a name few rivals dare test. Paradoxically, Jackson enforces a strict policy against violent crime within his territory, a choice that has won him the genuine loyalty and protection of the mortal residents, who consider him a hero and warn him of any trespassers before Kindred threats even arrive. His domain stands as a rare example of Kindred rule that mortals actively welcome, and a useful contact or obstacle for coteries operating on Chicago's South Side.

Patricia of Bollingbroke rose from the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381, where grief over her murdered husband and stolen children hardened her into one of the rebellion's true guiding voices alongside her lover, Wat Tyler. Condemned after the revolt's collapse, she was Embraced in a dungeon cell by a seventh-generation @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} calling himself Robin, and took her freedom by killing the baron responsible for her family's destruction. Centuries later, having drunk deeply and repeatedly of an ancient vampire's blood without realizing the danger, she found herself Blood Bound to Helena, who valued her as a ruthless assassin. Helena's secret backing, combined with Patricia's own age and intelligence, earned her a respected seat among Chicago's Brujah elders — a position she cemented during the Council Wars by slaying a descendant of Critias who defied the primogen's will. She and Critias despise each other bitterly, a rivalry sharpened on his side by simple hatred and on hers by an open hunger for his ancient vitae.

pages.name: Notable Locations: Elysium, the Rack, and the Succubus Club

text.content:
Elysium is declared across several rotating sites in Chicago (including the Museum of Contemporary Art), governed by strict Traditions of neutrality; even Balthazar, the Sheriff, has been known to stake out the museum after hours to catch anarchs violating decorum, though direct enforcement inside Elysium itself is heavily frowned upon.

The Rack is a stretch of the city known as neutral hunting and socializing ground for Kindred of every sect and status, where elders and anarchs alike can be found feeding, dealing, and posturing without violating Elysium's stricter rules; Balthazar is frequently found there, well-dressed, when not busy intimidating rivals elsewhere.

The Succubus Club is one of Chicago's most storied Kindred haunts, a nightclub steeped in decades of @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador}-flavored decadence and intrigue, long a site of political maneuvering, seduction, and secret alliance-building among the city's elite.

vtmlarp.source: Chicago by Night, 2nd Edition, Chapters One, Two, and Four
